newsitem.title: CANADA: Hydro-Quebec okays U.S. power sales in Quebec.
newsitem.headline: Hydro-Quebec okays U.S. power sales in Quebec.

text.p: In a step that would end Hydro-Quebec's monopoly on electricity sales in Quebec, it is proposing that U.S. electricity producers be allowed to sell power in the Canadian province.

According to documents filed with the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, Hydro-Quebec is proposing that any North American electricity producer be allowed to sell directly to the utility or nine Quebec municipalities and one cooperative that have their own distribution networks in the province.
Quebec government-owned Hydro-Quebec generates, transmits and distributes most of the electricity consumed in Quebec.

In its previous application, Hydro-Quebec proposed that U.S. producers be allowed only "wheel-through" transmission in Quebec, meaning they would be able to use Hydro-Quebec's power grid only to distribute electricity to non-Quebec buyers.

Under its modified application, "transmission of electricity from Quebec (wheel-out), transmission across the province (wheel-through) and transmission of electricity into the province (wheel-in) are all permissible," it said.
"In short, the revised tariff provides U.S. entities the same access to Quebec's grid and wholesale customers as those U.S. entities provide to Hydro-Quebec," its filing said.
Hydro-Quebec's amended application focuses on seeking reciprocity in access to electricity transmission networks in the United States and Quebec.

Hydro-Quebec operates generating facilities having a total capacity of more than 31,000 MW. The utility's annual deliveries are in excess of 166 billion kilowatthours, of which almost 24 billion kilowatthours are exported to neighboring Canadian provinces and the United States.
On Thursday, Hydro-Quebec reiterated that it "plans to seize business opportunities resulting from the restructuring of the continental energy market."
Hydro-Quebec has a 47 percent interest in Noverco Inc, a holding company which indirectly holds an 80 percent interest in Gaz Metropolitain and Co LP, Quebec's main natural gas distributor.
Gaz Met controls 100 percent of Northern New England Gas Corp, a U.S. subsidiary which owns Vermont Gas Systems, a natural gas distributor in Vermont.

The nine municipalities, which include the cities of Westmount in metropolitan Montreal, and Sherbrooke and Magog in the province's Eastern Townships near the Vermont border, distribute about two percent of the electricity consumed in the province.

Hydro-Quebec's proposal is part of a modified application to the FERC filed on Tuesday in which the utility is seeking the right to sell electricity at market prices in American markets. As a concession to U.S. producers, Hydro-Quebec is proposing that they be allowed to sell electricity to Hydro-Quebec or the province's 10 independent distributors.
